tldr: Azure's Markdown for Agents preview reportedly cuts web responses by 97% at the median, potentially reducing agent token costs and input noise.
OpenAI is reaffirming zero data retention for eligible API customers and previewing private safety processing, which matters for enterprise data-boundary decisions.
Azure's GA VM controls let you disable hyper-threading or constrain cores, creating new performance and software-licensing options for selected workloads.

top.title: Azure GA adds VM controls for hyper-threading and core counts
top.summary: Azure now generally supports disabling Simultaneous Multithreading/Hyper-Threading and configuring constrained core counts on supported VM sizes. The controls provide one thread per physical core and more control over the vCPU configuration.
top.why: Re-run performance and licensing models for workloads where predictable physical-core exposure or per-core software licensing matters, but first verify support for the target VM sizes.

top.title: Azure App Service previews Markdown responses for AI agents
top.summary: Markdown for Agents removes browser-oriented scripts, styles, and markup before returning web content to an agent; Microsoft says a test across more than 637,000 pages produced responses that were 97% smaller at the median, with a median conversion time of two milliseconds.
top.why: Consider it for web-grounded agents because smaller inputs can reduce token spend and context pressure, while validating that the conversion does not remove content your application needs.

top.title: Azure API Management expands its AI Gateway tier for agents
top.summary: The new API Management AI Gateway tier is positioned as the data path for App Service-hosted agents, providing model access, token limits, semantic caching, token metrics, and an MCP traffic contract alongside Foundry's gateway control plane.
top.why: Revisit whether model routing, token governance, caching, and MCP controls belong in a shared APIM gateway rather than being implemented separately in each agent.

top.title: Azure Site Recovery GA lets failovers reuse a prebuilt NIC
top.summary: Azure-to-Azure Site Recovery now supports attaching an existing, pre-provisioned network interface in the target region during test failover and failover, preserving prepared networking configurations.
top.why: Update disaster-recovery runbooks and infrastructure templates where stable private IP, NSG, or other NIC configuration is important during AI-service failover.

also.title: Azure Databricks Lakebase reaches GA in four more regions
also.summary: Lakebase is now generally available in North Central US, France Central, Germany West Central, and East Asia, adding regional deployment options.

top.title: OpenAI reaffirms zero data retention for eligible API customers
top.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed Zero Data Retention for eligible API customers and previewed Private Safety Processing, intended to support advanced safety measures without exposing customer data for retention.
top.why: Use the eligibility and processing details when deciding whether sensitive workloads can use frontier models, rather than assuming every API deployment receives the same privacy treatment.

top.title: AI inference costs increasingly depend on the whole data-center stack
top.summary: A report on production inference argues that GPU throughput is only one part of the system: storage latency, network bandwidth, data movement, and power increasingly determine token speed and cost, with different trade-offs for interactive and batch workloads.
top.why: Benchmark complete serving architectures—including storage, networking, power, and queueing—instead of selecting GPUs from model throughput numbers alone.

top.title: Stripe agrees to acquire OpenRouter in a reported $7.5B deal
top.summary: Stripe said it agreed to acquire model-routing startup OpenRouter, while reported valuations of $7.5 billion or more remain unconfirmed and differ between reports.
top.why: Treat the deal as a signal that model routing is becoming strategic infrastructure, and monitor ownership, pricing, and provider-neutrality risks before making OpenRouter a central dependency.

also.title: Marvell shares rise after disclosing a Google AI-chip design deal
also.summary: Marvell disclosed a Google AI-chip design contract and a warrant allowing Google to purchase about 59 million shares valued at $12.2 billion.

top.title: DeepSeek open-sources a modular runtime for autonomous agents
top.summary: DeepSeek released developer-preview DeepSeek Harness (dsh), an open-source execution runtime with a micro-kernel architecture, pluggable functional modules, and append-only event logging. It is positioned as an alternative to more tightly coupled agent frameworks, but its plugin ecosystem and API maintenance are unproven.
top.why: Evaluate it only in a controlled agent-infrastructure pilot if modular execution and auditability are priorities; the developer-preview status makes it unsuitable for a foundational production dependency today.

top.title: Codex agents can continue working while awaiting developer input
top.summary: Codex now supports asynchronous progress when a long-running coding agent needs an answer, allowing it to continue other work instead of stopping completely while it waits for developer input.
top.why: Reconsider agent job orchestration and approval boundaries because unattended progress requires stronger workspace isolation, checkpointing, and review controls.
